annotations.title: Look up one security control, verbatim

description: What does this security control actually require? Give a control number and get that provision's text exactly as its publisher prints it, with the citation, the source URL and the publisher's own page. Covers five published documents: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 (e.g. "SC-28", "AC-2a", "AU-6(1)"), NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3, the requirements CMMC assesses against (e.g. "03.05.03", "03.01.01.c.02"), NIST SP 800-218, the Secure Software Development Framework (e.g. "PW.7.2", "PO.1.1"), the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (e.g. "GV.OC-01", "PR.AA-05"). The HIPAA Security Rule, 45 CFR part 164 subpart C (164.302 to 164.318), is held and NOT served: our own copy was collected from a path ecfr.gov's robots.txt disallows, so those citations answer that we do not publish them, say why, and link the rule itself. One record is one obligation, so a control with lettered statements answers per statement, and the sub-provisions under the one you asked for are listed by citation. Where NIST leaves a value to the reading organisation its text prints a placeholder, so those provisions come back twice: "requirement" is the publisher's bytes with the placeholder in them, and "requirement_resolved" is the same sentence with each placeholder replaced by the catalogue's own label or choice list, in square brackets -- readable, and still visibly a value you have to decide. A control number we do not hold returns "not in our records" -- never a paraphrase and never a guess. SOC 2, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS are deliberately absent: that text is copyrighted by the bodies that sell it.

framework.description: Optional. Assert which document you meant: "nist" for NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, "nist-800-171" for NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3, "ssdf" for NIST SP 800-218, "csf" for the NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, "hipaa" for the HIPAA Security Rule. The five numbering schemes do not collide, so this is only needed to be told when a control number belongs to another one.

id.description: The control number as the publisher cites it, e.g. "SC-28", "SC-28(1)", "AC-2a", "03.05.03", "PW.7.2", "GV.OC-01", "164.312(a)(2)(iv)". A leading "45 CFR", a section sign or "NIST SP 800-53" is ignored, and case does not matter.
